key_insight: QPipe uses an LLM-driven multi-agent workflow to convert natural-language requirements into executable quantum applications for test optimization, reducing the need for deep quantum expertise.
engineering_relevance: The approach suggests a practical path for automating quantum software generation in software engineering tasks where traceability, execution, and solution quality matter.
method: Multi-agent pipeline: requirement parsing, formulation, code generation, review, execution, verification
Generates traceable quantum-application workflows from natural-language task descriptions
Supports iterative refinement through agent coordination and feedback
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 20 real-world benchmark requirements, QPipe averaged 100% code compilation and 96.7% successful execution/final-result combination, with average generation cost of 260.1 seconds and 1.89M tokens per requirement.
watch_item: Results depend on preserving code-generation skill, task knowledge, review feedback, and multi-agent decomposition, so performance may drop if any stage is weakened.
paper_title: Leveraging LLM-Based Agentic Systems to Generate Quantum Applications for Test Optimization
